name: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
description: MTEB is a benchmark for text embeddings spanning 8 embedding tasks (bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, semantic textual similarity, and summarization) covering a total of 58 datasets and 112 languages. It provides a comprehensive evaluation framework for text embedding models, including open-source code and a public leaderboard.
creator: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers
citeAs: Muennighoff, N., Tazi, N., Magne, L., & Reimers, N. MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark.
rai:dataCollection: Datasets were collected from a variety of sources including public APIs (arXiv, bioRxiv, medRxiv), existing NLP benchmarks (BEIR, SemEval, SentEval), Kaggle competitions, Reddit posts, StackExchange posts, and other publicly available datasets. Custom datasets were created for MTEB using these public APIs and data sources.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include: arXiv public API, bioRxiv/medRxiv APIs, Reddit posts, StackExchange posts, Amazon customer reviews, Twitter messages, online banking queries, news articles, scientific papers, question-answer forums (AskUbuntu, StackOverflow), and various existing NLP benchmark datasets (BEIR, SemEval STS datasets, BUCC, Tatoeba, etc.).
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For ArxivClustering, multiple categories can be given to a single paper so only the first one is used. For S2S datasets, input text is the title of the paper; for P2P, input text is the concatenation of title and abstract. For ArxivClustering, three types of splits are created: main category clustering, secondary category clustering within the same main category, and secondary category clustering across all main categories. Subsets of labels are selected and articles are sampled from those labels to yield splits with varying amounts and sizes of clusters.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Datasets are grouped into three categories based on text length: Sentence to sentence (S2S), Paragraph to paragraph (P2P), and Sentence to paragraph (S2P). Models are evaluated on test splits of all datasets except MSMARCO where the dev split is used. MTEB imposes no limit on input length, leaving it up to the models to truncate if necessary. Versioning is applied at dataset and software level for reproducibility.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Cluster labels for arXiv, bioRxiv, and medRxiv datasets are generated using categories given to the papers by humans. For bioRxiv and medRxiv, the category is unique per paper; for arXiv, multiple categories can be assigned and only the first is used. Other datasets use annotations from their original sources (e.g., SemEval STS scores from 0-5, binary labels for pair classification, intent/scenario labels for MASSIVE datasets, counterfactual/toxicity labels for classification datasets).
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Mini-batch k-means (scikit-learn, batch size 32) for clustering evaluation; logistic regression classifier (scikit-learn, 100 maximum iterations) for classification evaluation.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: MTEB is open-source with versioning at dataset and software level. Datasets and results are available on the Hugging Face Hub. The benchmark welcomes task, dataset, or metric contributions from the community via pull requests. A public leaderboard is maintained at https://huggingface.co/spaces/mteb/leaderboard with automatic submission format.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MTEB aims to simplify the selection of text embedding models for practitioners and researchers, potentially accelerating progress toward universal text embeddings applicable across diverse tasks and languages. By providing a comprehensive benchmark, it reduces the risk of blindly applying models to unsuitable use cases in industry.
rai:dataBiases: MTEB average scores are biased towards tasks with many datasets, notably retrieval, classification, and clustering, due to task imbalance (e.g., summarization consists of only a single dataset). Retrieval and clustering datasets are English-only, limiting multilingual evaluation. Data contamination between MTEB datasets and model training datasets is not controlled for, as the scale of experiments and model pre-training makes this challenging.
rai:dataLimitations: 1. Long document datasets are missing; the longest datasets have a few hundred words. 2. Task imbalance: summarization has only one dataset, biasing average scores toward retrieval, classification, and clustering. 3. Multilinguality: retrieval and clustering are English-only; no code datasets are included. 4. Additional modalities (e.g., image content) are not covered. MTEB does not contain code datasets for benchmarking code models.
rai:dataUseCases: MTEB is intended for benchmarking and evaluating text embedding models across diverse tasks including bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, semantic textual similarity, and summarization. It supports model selection for industry and research applications, and serves as a foundation for future embedding research. Use cases include Training evaluation, Testing, and Zero-shot evaluation of embedding models.
